messages:
cheng: Heads-up — after the last runtime change (dynamic kernel pick + continuous batching tweak), we've started seeing slow memory growth on long-context requests. P99 latency also creeped up for a small subset of heavy sessions. I profiled a canary run and it looks like KV cache fragmentation + aggressive batch merging is causing head-of-line stalls when a huge context merges with small ones.

maria: Can you paste the top-level repro + short flamegraph snapshot?

cheng: Paste of the short repro and perf highlights below. TL;DR: when a long-session (16k tokens) hits and continuous-batcher merges it into a head batch, several subsequent batches block waiting on KV page fetches and the KV allocator fragments. Seen with both LRU and our generational eviction.

alex: +1 saw similar in my local run. Flame: most CPU in kv_pager::fetch_pages and kv_alloc::split_slab; long-tail allocs from "kv_fragment_merge" path. P99 token latency jumps ~40% in that scenario.

sam: very useful. Do you have the pprof flame snippet or top functions?

cheng: Here — top from pprof (sample-based):

```
pprof: top functions
20.3%  kv_pager::fetch_pages
15.6%  kv_alloc::split_slab
12.1%  continuous_batch::merge_batches
9.8%   kv_cache::evict_candidate_scan
8.4%   runtime::apply_attention_kernels
```

Also saw lots of small allocations pinned in a few slabs (fragmentation heatmap attached in the canary).

maria: Interesting that kernel selection appears in the trace — maybe fetch stalls are widening kernel choice windows and then we pick a non-ideal kernel?

alex: yep. When the batch merge increases its sequence window, runtime sometimes switches to a kernel variant (e.g., alt-attn) with different memory pattern and KV page layout expectations. That amplifies fragmentation and causes more page faults on our pager layer.

sam: Quick hypothesis list: 1) merge-window is too permissive (merges long contexts with many small ones) 2) merge scheduler doesn't consider KV residency (prefer to merge resident-key batches) 3) eviction policy not favoring consolidation of slabs -> fragmentation grows

cheng: Agreed. Proposed experiments:
- Temporarily reduce continuous_batch.merge_window_ms from 25 -> 5 for a canary region
- Add merge_priority_residency boolean so the batcher prefers merging batches with higher KV residency (cheap to serve)
- Add a backpressure knob: if a candidate batch touches > X distinct kv-pages, disallow merge

sam: +1. We should also run an A/B with eviction policy switch: LRU -> compaction-first (scan small slabs and compact before eviction) to measure memory growth.

alex: I pushed a quick config override for canary:

```
{"continuous_batch": {"merge_window_ms": 5, "max_merge_size": 6, "prefer_resident_kv": true, "merge_page_threshold": 64}}
```

infra-bot: deploybot: started canary roll (cluster: us-west-2-canary, config: cb-residency-2165439999) — build id 2026.3.21-rc4

maria: For metrics, let's track: kv_page_fault_rate, kv_fragmentation_ratio, p99_token_latency, batch_merge_rate, avg_batch_size. Also capture flamegraphs and heap profiles every 5m during the canary.

cheng: I'll own the canary run and collect profiles. Plan: 2h ramp, 6h steady-state, then rollback if kv_fragmentation_ratio > 1.2x baseline or p99 latency > +20% baseline.

alex: Also add a short-lived probe: a synthetic long-context session that repeatedly appends + truncates to exercise KV reclaim; collect per-slab occupancy traces.

sam: If the canary looks good, next step is to implement a smarter merge heuristic: score = (resident_page_fraction * w1) - (distinct_page_count * w2) + (batch_priority_bonus). Keep weights configurable.

cheng: I'll run the canary now. Posting quick checklist:
- [ ] start canary (done by infra-bot)
- [ ] attach flame/prof capture (cheng)
- [ ] run synthetic long-context probe (alex)
- [ ] monitor metrics (maria)
- [ ] decide: rollback or promote and code deeper fix (team)

maria: Thanks. Please ping #eng-sre if we see capacity noise. :eyes:

cheng: Updating thread with first 30m snapshot in ~35m.

alex: If we land the scoring heuristic later, we should also expose telemetry: why two batches merged (residency vs latency) so we can debug in-prod decisions.

sam: good point. add a small audit log line on merge decisions for 1% sampling.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary finished rollout to 3/3 nodes (us-west-2-canary).

cheng: First 35m snapshot: merge_rate down ~40%, kv_page_fault_rate down ~52%, p99_token_latency back near baseline. Fragmentation_ratio still slightly up (+7%) — looks like we reduced new fragmentation but not healed existing slabs. Will keep running.

maria: Nice. Keep the canary going and let's reconvene tomorrow to decide the codepath change. :thumbsup:

alex: saved some heap profiles to s3://redwood-inference/canaries/2165439999/ — I'll post links in a follow-up.

cheng: Thanks all. If canary stays clean I'll open a small PR to add the residency scoring and the merge_page_threshold protection.

sam: SGTM.

cheng: closing for now, will update later.
